title: thermite-lower: L1 exec-twin bytes_eq operand &-strip gap (build-side #279 mirror)
description:
SPILLOVER from #276 (Arc 2 editor content pins). #279 fixed the L3 SPEC byteview lowering of field-access bytes_eq operands. The L1 EXEC-TWIN call-site lowering has the analogous gap, UNFIXED.

ROOT CAUSE: thermite-lower/src/l1.rs::lower_expr_exec, Expr::Call string-arg arm. For a leading string arg it emits '{lowered}.clone()' where lowered=lower_expr_exec(arg). When the operand carries a leading & (&result.text / &ins / &b.text), lowered='&result.text' so '&result.text.clone()' parses as &(result.text.clone())=&TString, against the twin's owned param 'fn bytes_eq(a: TString, b: TString, ...)'. rustc E0308 at every &-prefixed conjunct. The C5/C7 comment's claim '(&TString).clone() yields owned TString' holds only when lowered is a bare ident.

REPRO: forge build a fn whose ens names bytes_eq(&result.text, &b.text, ...) over a Buf-wrapped String, --entry a no-param caller -> E0308 xN. The bare-field form 'result.text' builds clean (why #276 ships bare-field).

FIX: strip a single leading & from lowered before .clone() in the string-arg branch (exec-twin counterpart of #279's spec &-strip); cover &path/&field as #279 did spec-side.

IMPACT: low — both spec+exec accept the BARE forms, so #276 ships with the sanctioned bare-field spelling; the demo/REQ-18 &-prefixed spelling is currently check-only. Closing this makes the operand class build-symmetric.
